This is a nice video with idealistic views that should be true. But doesn't take into account the greed of massive companies who look for any way to remove jobs to increase their bottom line. Or the fact that pay usually doesn't follow an increase in productivity. So if a person can be 10% more productive in a company that doesn't mean they will get a 10% pay bump. And the company can look at that and say "we can fire every 10th worker and still have the same output while paying the other nine the same". AI may not remove jobs entirely, you will still need skilled works for so many of the fields that AI will effect, but it will surely reduce the total amount of jobs by a fair bit in the end I would think.
